segments.spokenText: Part 2. A guide to the town’s open-building weekend. You now have one minute to read questions 11 to 20.

Welcome to the information session for our open-building weekend. Several places normally closed to the public will offer visits, and the arrangements differ between sites. Please don't assume that the ticket for one building lets you enter all the others. Most visits are free, but we still need to manage numbers and protect working spaces. I'll explain five buildings first, then some general advice for planning your day. The leaflet contains addresses, and the updated website has the latest cancellation information.

segments.spokenText: The old courthouse is popular because people want to see the hearing room and the cells below. Only a limited number can enter each tour, so you must reserve a timed place before the weekend. We won't maintain a queue for spare places at the door. If you can't attend, cancel so someone else can use it. Booking several times in the hope of deciding later makes this much harder.

segments.spokenText: The clock workshop is reached by a steep staircase. There is no lift, and the narrow turn means we cannot install a temporary ramp. The ground-floor display remains available to everyone, but a visit to the workshop itself involves stairs. The leaflet states this clearly because we don't want someone travelling across town only to discover the restriction on arrival.

segments.spokenText: At the recording studio, visitors can try making a short sound effect under supervision. Bring nothing special; the materials are supplied. The session is designed around participation rather than standing silently while someone describes equipment. Your recording can be sent to you afterwards if you choose to provide an address, but you don't have to give one to take part.

segments.spokenText: The water tower offers the best view, but its opening depends on conditions. Strong wind makes the exposed upper platform unsuitable for visitors. Check the morning update before leaving home. We don't cancel just because it's cloudy, but safety takes priority over keeping a promise printed weeks earlier. A closure there doesn't mean every other building will be closed.

segments.spokenText: The municipal greenhouse will stay open later than the other sites, until eight in the evening. That may help people who work during the day. Please use the marked paths because staff will still be maintaining plants in some sections. You can see those activities, but the site isn't being converted into an unrestricted evening park.

segments.spokenText: For travel, we recommend the temporary circular bus. A ticket covers repeated journeys during the day, and the bus stops near all five sites. Walking between two nearby buildings is easy, but the whole circuit is longer than it appears on the small leaflet map. The service is intended to make combinations possible, not to require visitors to see every location in one day.

segments.spokenText: Please arrive for a reserved tour about ten minutes early. Earlier than that, there may be nowhere suitable to wait. A guide cannot delay the start for late arrivals because the next group needs its own full visit. If you miss a start, contact the booking desk rather than attempting to join through a side entrance.

segments.spokenText: Photography rules vary. You may photograph public displays where signs permit, but working documents on desks are not part of the exhibition. Ask before taking an identifiable photograph of an employee. Some are doing their ordinary jobs while visits take place, and being visible to the public isn't agreement to appear in somebody's online album.

segments.spokenText: Children are welcome on the family routes shown in the leaflet. Other tours include lengthy explanations or restricted spaces, so please read the age guidance. It isn't a judgement about whether a particular child is well behaved. It's information about what the organiser can provide safely and comfortably within that building.

segments.spokenText: At the end of a visit, you may be invited to suggest questions for next year's programme. We particularly want to know what you'd like to understand about the work done inside these buildings. Requests simply to open more places are welcome, but a specific question helps us plan a useful visit rather than merely unlock another door. Staff have volunteered their time, and good questions make the exchange rewarding for them too.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 2. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
